items.title: AskChief: The end of shipmanagement’s institutional memory problem?
points: Michalis Gkontas, co-founder and CEO of AskChief, explains how artificial intelligence could fundamentally change the way ships are managed at sea and ashore, turning years of fragmented operational knowledge into an instantly accessible resource.

The future of shipmanagement will be less dependent on individual experience, institutional memory and the availability of particular people, according to Michalis Gkontas, co-founder and CEO of maritime AI specialist AskChief.
“AI will make shipmanagement less dependent on who happens to be available or who remembers what happened last time,” he says.
For Gkontas, the transformation will come not from replacing experienced superintendents or seafarers but from giving them immediate access to information accumulated across a company’s fleet.
“Company systems will become more than passive archives,” he says.
“At sea, crews will be able to access relevant documentation and previous experience while a problem is unfolding.

items.title: Dollar hedging by Indian companies slumps as RBI cracks down on speculation
points: Indian companies cut dollar purchases used to hedge against rupee weakness to an eight-month low, a sign that the central bank’s crackdown on what it called speculative bets against the currency is yielding results.

Buying of forward dollars, or commitments by companies to acquire the US currency at a later date, fell 35 per cent in October from a record high the previous month to $49.5 billion, according to clearinghouse data.
The figure was the lowest since February and reflects hedging by importers against losses from a weaker rupee.
The drop followed sweeping measures by the Reserve Bank of India last month to defend the rupee as it neared a record low.

The steps, which include a China-style foreign-exchange risk reserve, have made it more expensive to build forward dollar positions, helping ease pressure on the rupee even as costly oil continues to the strain India’s external finances.
The currency has since risen about 2 per cent against the dollar.

items.title: Gadkari Confirms E100 Innova HyCross Launch This Month
points: Union Road Transport Minister Nitin Gadkari says he will launch Toyota's ethanol-powered Innova HyCross in November 2026.
Gadkari made the announcement at the ENRich 2026 conference in New Delhi on November 2.
Toyota Kirloskar Motor unveiled an Innova HyCross-based electrified flex-fuel prototype in August 2023.
On October 26, the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways amended the Central Motor Vehicles Rules to include E100 in the certification framework for flex-fuel vehicles.
Gadkari also named Tata Motors, Mahindra, Suzuki and Hyundai among manufacturers working on ethanol-compatible vehicles.
Maruti Suzuki has already introduced the WagonR Bioflex, although Business Today reports only 20 registrations since its June 2026 launch.
A flexible-fuel vehicle can use other approved blends, which helps, but the case for paying extra for E100 capability becomes weaker if pure ethanol is not available near the owner.
Gadkari cited ethanol at about Rs 75 per litre against petrol at roughly Rs 120.

items.title: Telangana conductor pushed from moving bus amid argument over change dies
points: A 24-year-old Telangana State Road Transport Corporation (TGSRTC) conductor, who sustained critical injuries after allegedly being pushed out of a bus during an altercation over change, died at a hospital in Hyderabad late on Tuesday.
Police inspector Ch Yellaiah said a passenger, Mounika, allegedly pushed Gundla Pravalika from the moving bus on October 25, and the conductor came under its rear wheels.
He added that Mounika boarded the bus with her son and said she was entitled to free travel under a government scheme.
Mounika agreed to buy a full ticket for ₹10.
She paid the conductor a ₹100 note and demanded immediate return of ₹90.
“As Pravalika had no change, she asked Mounika to collect the balance while getting off the bus.
The RTC workers’ Joint Action Committee (JAC) demanded justice for her family and called for a shutdown of bus depots across the Khammam region.
Srinivasa Rao is Senior Assistant Editor based out of Hyderabad covering developments in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana .

items.title: VinFast VF MPV 7 Price Cut Rs 4.1 Lakh – Now Costs Rs 20.39 Lakh
